XEN COMPANION 2.0.0-beta.11: TECHNICAL NOTES
===========================================

Everything about how Xens work, what changed, the settings and the commands. The short version is on the release page.


WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.11
===========================

Hardcore (XenConfig.hardcore: "auto" | "on" | "off"; hardcore(server) is on, or auto and server.isHardcore()):
- Personality.lifeWeight (1.4 hardcore, else 1) multiplies cautionScale(); XenMod.tickWorld sets it and re-applies every
  Xen's personality when it changes (emotions.baseCaution comes from it).
- Companion.died: hardcore and not in the arena -> lore "<name> died for good (<death message>)", goneIn = 40 ticks, no
  respawn. goneForGood: the body leaves the player list, mod.forget, XenMod.goneForGood: Roster.forget (nothing kept:
  that name is someone new next time), away list, a grey "[Xen] <name> is gone for good" to players, and every Xen that
  knew it (known or trust) notes it; those that liked it (trust > 0.3) within 64 blocks say so.
- refusal: hardcore, an errand that goes out (explore, wood, stone, coal, iron, mine, food) and health under 60%: no,
  before "please" is looked at. Dragon.heal backs off 4 health sooner. The chat notes end "You have only one life: if
  you die, you are gone for good."
Persona (talk/Chat.PERSONA, the same in xen/talk/chat.py and the crossCheck fixture): "a player living in this
Minecraft world", knows only what it saw, remembers or was told, guesses about far things, may not know; own goals,
friends and fears; can say no. A fourth example: "are you a bot?" -> "No, I'm Xen. I live out here, same as you."
Chat.OUTSIDE (ai, artificial intelligence, language model, chatbot, bot, npc, program, assistant) throws a reply away
like a made-up one (one more try, then its own words). SmallTalk's bot answers stay in the world.
Village houses (VillageHouses.java):
- The game's own files: structure/village/<kind>/houses/<kind>_{small,medium,big}_house_<n>.nbt, opened by name from
  the server's resource manager (26.3 changed listResources), read with a small NBT reader (palette, blocks, size).
  Jigsaw and structure blocks are left out. The door's lower half gives the front (the edge of the house it's nearest).
- designOf: footprint, wall height (door to the first layer that's mostly stairs and slabs), roof (stairs facing 4
  ways above the door: hip, 2: gable, else flat), stone base and bottom row, logs (frame), trapdoors (shutters),
  fences (porch, yard), leaves, ladder (loft), flowers or farmland (garden), water (pond), work blocks (workshop).
- loose(): blocks of the shell that can't be reached from the bottom layer through faces (igloo domes held up by snow
  layers): a house with any isn't copied (3 of the 18 snowy ones).
- Seeing a village (Structures: a bell): kindOf(biome) (desert, savanna, snowy/ice/frozen, taiga/grove, else plains);
  Taste.admire 2 of its houses (+0.08 to each of their design choices) and liking "seen:<kind>" = 1 (kept with taste).
- Taste.copies(): seen any, and like("copy:village") + noise(+-0.25) > 0; its prior is 0.3 - 0.6 curiosity. Asked
  ("village house", "house like the village", "village-style": Chat.houseStyle and chat.py) it copies anyway (the
  biome's kind if it has seen none). Not for a first house in survival. builtCopy -> built + copy liking toward how it
  went; praise and criticism move the copy liking too.
- plan(): rotate the house so its door side faces front (positions and block states), place it in the site's box (the
  door one above the floor), air above the floor dug, decor (beds, torches, glass, flowers, work blocks...) last and
  optional, the shell in one phase from the ground up. Survival: adapt() (its own wood for any wood; stripped logs and
  wood to logs; stone, bricks, sandstone, smooth stone, snow block and packed ice to cobblestone and its stairs, slabs,
  walls; terracotta, wool, clay and concrete to planks; grass and sand to dirt), and only houses on flat ground (door
  at most 2 up), at most 13 across, nine tenths of them of what it can make.
From the run that beat the game (aibengineering/beat-the-game-minecraft, CC BY 4.0; looked at in scratch, not kept):
387 actions, 15 crystal attempts (8 open crystals by bow, 2 misses; 2 caged ones: bow failed twice, then 36 end stone
up and a sword), 4 bow shots at the flying dragon (all missed), 13 perched attacks (about 26 damage each), dragon
breath over the standing spot (waited), down to 0.68 health, 40 blocks away and back full; a bed slept in 4 blocks from
the stronghold portal before going in.
- Knowledge: dragon_perch (0.5), end_retreat (0.6), end_bed (0.5).
- Dragon.shootHer: arrows used while shooting her in the air (inventory) and her health falling then (not perched);
  shoots only while (hits + 1) / (shots + told + 2) >= 0.3, told = 4 if it knows dragon_perch; 3 shots, no hit: it
  learns it (TRIED).
- Dragon.heal: knows end_retreat (or learns it at 4 health) and health <= 6 + 4 (1 - bravery) (+4 hardcore): off to
  40 blocks from the middle on the far side from her, eating while food < 20, back at max health - 2.
- headHit: a breath cloud within its radius + 1.5 of the spot: it waits radius + 3 out, glancing.
- Blocks: Hands.PLACEABLE and SPARE_FIRST have netherrack and end_stone. In the End with under 32 blocks (and a
  pickaxe) it mines 48 end stone; a caged crystal needs (pillar top - ground beside it) + 14; short, it mines what's
  missing + 8. Adventure.prepared() wants 64 blocks (was 128 cobblestone or dirt).
- Adventure.bedByPortal (knows end_bed): its bed put down beside it at the portal (Companion.bedRoom) and used (a bed
  sets the respawn point by day too), once, before going in.
Head turning (Hands.turnToward), fitted to OpenBlock-Team/Minecraft-Navigation and Minecraft-ChopTree (CC BY 4.0;
200 + 50 runs at 20 a second, looked at in scratch, not kept): their mouse turns took 5 ticks for 9 degrees, 8 for 40,
11 for 80, 16 for 160, the fastest tick about 0.2 of the turn and barely any of it in the first tick. Now a speed per
axis: toward sqrt(2 a e) (no faster than it can stop in), at most a = 2.2 degrees a tick more or less each tick
(TURN_ACCEL, times the reaction setting's turn scale), capped by the caller's maximum; a turn that stopped starts from
still. The model gives 3, 5, 7, 10 and 15 ticks for those turns. Watching someone (not in a fight) turns the same way.
Their block snapshots stop at 4096 blocks counted from one edge of the box, so they can't be its senses: Ex1 is not
retrained on them.
Watching (XenMod.watchedBreak): a player (not a Xen) breaks an ore; Xens within 24 blocks that can see them:
Lessons.watched moves the belief up to 4 blocks toward that height (0.15 x trust, less with 3 own finds), a little
surer each time, teacher = that player.
Builder.onSite: in its plan's box (a block around). Chores.gather (what it knows) and the gathering step (what it
glances and what it remembers) skip blocks there.


WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.10
===========================

The recording (looked at in scratch, not kept): 290 s in the End. It took 39 hits: enderman 48.9 damage, the dragon
20.8, a fall 2.2. It swung at the dragon 22 times and at endermen 19. The fling came at 45.7 s: velocity
(4.08, 2.83, 0) right after two jump hits on the perched dragon, from the exit portal under her head. Then pitch 79
and an ender pearl at 47.3 s, and landing at 48.7 s with 2.25 damage. Looking at the dragon: median 37 degrees off,
within 15 degrees 18% of the time. Endermen within 16: median 94 degrees off.
Dragon.java:
- headHit: it stands 3 blocks from her head, on the side away from her body (head minus body, flat, normalised), and
  walks there when more than 2.5 off or out of reach. Before, it walked to under the head.
- glance(dragon) while waiting for her to land: watching her 18 ticks in each 70. The rest, it holds a look at the
  ground 6 ahead. Before: watching = dragon, all the time.
Tactics:
- pearlTick (every tick, from Companion.tick right after the water clutch). It needs pearl_clutch (share 0.5) and a
  pearl, and to be falling (vy <= 0, not in water, not gliding), at most once in 30 ticks. The cooldown resets on
  landing.
  - lastGround is its position on the ground, only when a block is really under it (a teleport can say onGround in
    mid-air).
  - Off an edge first: lastGround within 30 across, between 12 above and 25 below it, and nothing under it within 6.
    The landing spot is the top of the block within 3 of lastGround with the most solid blocks around it (less 0.3 a
    block of distance). pearlAim flies pitches -60 to 60 (step 2) from just under the eyes, 1.5 a tick, gravity 0.03
    then drag 0.99 each tick, moving in quarters. Only a flight that comes down onto a block's top (free above)
    counts; the nearest to the spot within 4 is taken. A Xen's pearl gets none of its movement:
    Projectile.shootFromRotation adds getKnownMovement(), which for a ServerPlayer is lastKnownClientMovement. It
    starts at Vec3.ZERO, and only the network handler sets it.
  - Else, ground below within 64 and fall + depth >= 12 (vy < -0.3): Hands.throwAt(pearl, yaw, 90).
  - -Dxen.pearlDebug=true journals each throw's aim and where the pearl came down.
- Endermen (knows "endermen", born), every 4 ticks, not fighting: an enderman within 32 that isn't after it means a held
  look at the ground 3 ahead (about 30 degrees down), whichever way it turns. Companion.somethingToLookAt and the
  Habits glance leave endermen out.
Checked (scratch end_client.js):
- 40-block drops: alive at 17 to 18 health every run.
- Off a sky platform 8 blocks from each edge, 40 down: 6 of 6 back onto it ("off the edge: an ender pearl back to").
- The enderman 10 ahead at eye height: 0 to 5 of 20 samples within 14 degrees, varying from run to run.
- In the End the platform tests weren't reliable: with no player there, the forced chunks weren't always loaded in
  time for the fill. The pearls that were logged came down on the platform where they were aimed.


WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.9
==========================

Whims.java (Companion.instinct, right before Antics; free Xens with wants on):
- boredom 0 to 1. Each decision it rises by decisionTicks / (20 * 60 * (6 + 8 * patience)), so it is full after 6 to
  14 minutes. It rises twice as fast with no option or while "looking around". Each new option takes off 0.25.
  -Dxen.boredFast=true multiplies the rise by 200 (tests only).
- Full: resists()? Else a whim. A chore of its own is cancelled first; one it was asked to do counts as necessity 1.
  - The whims, weighted 0.2 + chattiness + 0.5 kindness (party), 0.2 + curiosity + 0.5 diligence (plan), 0.5 (needless).
  - Plan: one of 8 big things and one of 5 whens, said out loud, journal "plans" (nothing more: it may never happen).
  - Party (one in the world at a time): Whims.party = (host, here, 1 minute). Another free Xen within 48 joins with
    chance 0.4 + 0.6 chattiness, if it trusts the host 0.25 or more and isn't fighting or busy. It walks there and
    Antics.danceNow() within 4 of it till the party ends.
  - Needless: sort slots 9 to 35 by item name, or name a favourite from the blocks within 6 (not grass, dirt, stone).
- necessity(): 1 if asked (chores not own) or fighting/in danger. 0.9 for FOOD/EAT at food 6 or less (0.6 at 12 or
  less), and for SHELTER/SLEEP after sunDown. 0.8 for WOOD/CRAFT with no pickaxe, 0.6 for STONE/CRAFT under stone tools,
  0.4 for MINE/SMELT under iron. Else 0.
- willpower(): 0.25 + 0.4 diligence + 0.3 patience - 0.4 sloth, from 0.05 to 1.
- resists(): need 1, or a roll under need * (0.6 + willpower). Holding out sets boredom to 0.9. Journal "bored stiff,
  but keeps at it: <why>", at most every 2 minutes, and a line said. Habits.bored() (drop the same work after 5 to 15
  minutes) is now also false when resists().
Trust:
- Companion.refusal: no owner, trust under 0.3, not "peace". A roll under (0.3 - trust) * 2 + 0.3 (1 - kindness) gives
  "No, you won't: you don't know <who> well enough yet." This is under the refuse setting, as the other refusals.
- Needs.canHelp also needs trust(who) >= 0.35 - 0.3 kindness.
Trial chamber walls:
- Knowledge "trial_walls" (share 0.3; told with flat/straight/smooth ... wall(s) ... trial).
- Tactics, under the sky only, every 100 ticks, until it knows a trial chamber: look 2 to 16 blocks in each of the 4
  directions to the first solid block. Count the 5 wide x 4 high patch around it on that plane: base stone with air in
  front of every block (20 of 20) counts. Not when the air in front is on the way it walked (a room it dug). Then Places
  "trial chamber" 6 blocks behind the wall, which Goals' TRIALS short goal uses. Journal "notes a dead-flat wall".
  - Why: trial chambers use terrain adaptation "encapsulate", a solid shell, and caves stop at it.
  - Checked: a room carved in stone 25 blocks down gave "a dead-flat wall at 1300, 61, -714: a trial chamber behind it".
Map in its head: Walker.beenAt(pos) is the way memory (beta 7). Caves.sample counts a spot as seen when it's on the
way, or when its 4x4 cell was visited within 24000 ticks (it was 6000). A seen spot scores 30 less, so it goes on into
new tunnels.
Commands: XenMod.mayRun(source) checks for an operator, or the player whose name is the singleplayer profile's on a
world that isn't a dedicated server (single player, or the host of a LAN world). spawn, set, arena and the op()
checks use it. It can't be tested on a dedicated server: there it is operators only, as before.
Settings screen: a Basics tab first (chat, talk, maxPerPlayer, wants, pvp, nameStyle, skins, chatModel), with a "More
settings" / "Fewer settings" button. Opened on another tab, all of them show. The screenshot walk still goes through
every tab.


WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.8.1
============================

Tested in the game with a pass or fail check for each tactic (scratch test proof_client.js: a 25x25 glass-walled
arena, and a 9x4x3 stone block with a 7-long tunnel for the underground ones). The fixes:
- Companion.request: knowledge.heard(words) now runs right after requestWords, for anyone trusted 0.3 or more.
  heard() only takes mechanics it doesn't know yet, so a sentence about one it knows goes on as before. Before, it ran
  after the intent and opinion handlers: a sentence that matched a shelter request or an opinion never got there.
- Companion.instinct: tactics.next() moved to right after gut.override(). Before, it was after the water and shore
  reflexes, which took every tick with water at its feet.
- Fighter: a creeper with isIgnited() (flint and steel, or a command) is about to blow too, not only one with
  getSwellDir() > 0.
- Critters (an archer in sight, between its shots, the Xen armed): with skeleton_dodge, more than 4 away, it watches
  it and goes LEFT, FORWARD, RIGHT, FORWARD (8 ticks each), not straight at it. Fighter's version of this never ran
  for archers: Critters comes first.
- The test's own mistake, for the record: a Xen told "stay" walks back to where it was told, so each scene told it
  "stay" again where it was.
Results: water, lava, creeper (19 of 20 health after the blast), skeleton (a sideways wobble of -1.3 to +1.8 blocks,
3 turns), full bag, storm ("night: digging down to mine (safe under the ground)" right after it began): all pass.
Diamonds: 2 of 5 Xens said they had none.


WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.8
==========================

Knowledge (a player's answers):
- New mechanics, made with t(): born false, a chat pattern to be told it, share 0.6. seed() runs on the first knows()
  (the name isn't set when Knowledge is made). It gives each one with chance 0.6 from Random(name hash * 131 + 17), so
  the same Xen always knows the same ones. They are block_water, cover_lava, creeper_block, skeleton_dodge,
  phantoms_hide, powder_snow, storm_shelter, spawner_torch, spear_reach and combo_shield. They spread like the others
  (told in chat, Tribe sharing).
Tactics.java (in Companion.instinct, before critters.danger):
- powder_snow: isInPowderSnow, so mine the powder snow at head, then feet (every tick).
- Every 10 ticks, under the sky only, not in water or lava:
  - block_water: water in a replaceable block beside its feet or head, or above, gets placeAt(any), then walker.stop.
  - cover_lava: lava beside it (level, one down, one up) or under its feet gets placeAt(any).
- spawner_torch (every 40 ticks): a spawner within 4 (2 down, 3 up) goes into Places "spawner" (once, journal
  "notes"). A torch goes on top if the top is free and it carries one.
- Checked in game: "putting a torch on the spawner" (the torch was there), and "mining its way out of the powder
  snow" (its head block was mined).
Fighter:
- Hands.ready(axeFirst, d): beyond 3 and up to SPEAR_REACH 4.5, the spear; else as before. hit() uses it too. Before,
  hit() called ready() (sword first), which undid the axe picked for a raised shield.
- Holding a spear, reach is 4.5 when d >= 2, else 0. Too close (under 2, not hurt this tick), it steps BACK. Spacing
  with spear_reach is 3.6.
  - The 1.21.11 spear item has AttackRange(2.0, 4.5, 2.0, 6.5, 0.125, 0.5), from Item.Properties.spear.
  - Checked: iron spear and iron sword against a zombie. The spear at 3.4 to 2.7 blocks, the sword at 2.6 and closer,
    and the zombie was dead in about 10 s.
- Wind-charge smash: knows wind_charge and mace, carries both, attack ready, on the ground, foe within 3.5 and not
  above it, at most every 40 ticks. Hands.throwDown("wind_charge") sets pitch 90 and uses it. hit() already swaps to
  the mace when fallDistance > 1.5 and the foe is below.
  - MaceItem: SMASH_ATTACK_FALL_THRESHOLD 1.5. The bonus is 4 a block to 3, 2 a block to 8, then 1 a block, plus
    density. A smash cancels the attacker's fall damage.
  - Checked: one smash killed a 20-health zombie, using 1 of 8 wind charges.
- combo_shield: hurt again within 30 ticks counts up the combo. At 3 it holds the shield up for 20 ticks while not
  ready (shieldUntil). Any hit of its own resets the combo. This is the Theobald bot's tempshield (combo >= 3).
- creeper_block: a hissing creeper within 3. If charged and in reach: a hit and an S-tap. Else placeAt(any) on the
  block between them, else raiseShield. Else it runs, as before.
- skeleton_dodge: a skeleton, stray or bogged (by type id: the class moved between versions) more than 4 off. It
  walks at a point 3 ahead and 2.5 to the side, switching sides every 15 ticks.
MindSense: SHELTER is also allowed in a thunderstorm (storm_shelter), or with a phantom within 32 (phantoms_hide).
Habits.tossJunk: JUNK adds cobblestone (keeps 64), sand (16) and red sand. Sticks are no longer junk, and logs never
were.
Chores.give: a precious thing (diamond, emerald, netherite, totem) it has no more than keep + 2 of. With chance
greed, it says it has none (journal "lies").
Tiers.java: skill(HT1..LT5) is 1.0 minus 0.05 a rank (LT5 0.55). local() reads config/xen/tiers.txt (made with
notes). online() calls GET mctiers.com/api/search_profile/<name>. It takes the best of rankings.*.{tier, pos}, where
pos 0 is high. That host is blocked from the build machine, so the format is from MCTiers' public API and untested
here. XenMod.create sets the tier at the end of create (after skills.born or restore) for an account's name (from the
list, or typed in /xen summon). FIGHT becomes max(FIGHT, skill).
- Checked: tiers.txt "jeb_ HT1", then /xen summon jeb_ logged "jeb_ fights like a HT1 (fight skill 1.0)".
The Theobald PVP Practice world (looked at, not run): TheobaldTheBot is a Carpet fake player driven by a datapack
(87 functions). It has sword and crystal tactics only: crit jumps from 3.5 to 6, an 11-tick hit cooldown, S-taps and
W-taps, random strafing every 5 ticks, a jump reset at HurtTime 10, an axe swap on a raised shield, the shield after a
3-hit combo, and a pearl when the target is 7 or more off. Xen's Fighter already had all of these but the combo shield.
The maces (density, wind burst) and spears are only in its kit chests.


WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.7
==========================

Crafting:
- Crafter.orderNext: Pace.craftPrep(order) used to run before the table steps, and step() ran its own craftPrep
  ("a place for the table", "a crafting table"). Each reset prepFor, so an order that needed a table it hadn't placed
  never got past the wait. This hit the furnace, and the builder's doors, stairs and chests. Now the table steps
  come first, and craftPrep(order) runs only with the table near (or for a 2x2 recipe).
  - Checked: a Xen given 3 raw iron, coal and 8 cobblestone, with no table down. Before, it waited at "making
    furnace" for over 100 s. Now: furnace 61 s after the give, iron pickaxe 96 s, with the stone tools and torches
    made first.
- Chores.smeltNext: no furnace, and under 8 stone (cobblestone, cobbled deepslate or blackstone): it gets stone first
  (stone in sight, else the staircase down) instead of ordering a furnace it can't make.
Building:
- First house: Goals.firstHouseTime() is an iron pickaxe, or a stone pickaxe and livedDays() >= 2. Both the HOUSE
  short goal and the Mind's HOUSE option (MindSense) use it. The Mind's option only needed 60 wood before, so a day-1
  Xen with stone tools chose a house: "stone +42.3 house +44.5 wood +43.8".
- Palettes with no stone (Architect.ofWood with stoneBase false: the base is the log). TimberHouse and Architect.designed
  used the base for the lower walls, the wall fill and two layers of foundation under the edges. Now those are the
  wall block (planks), and there is no foundation under the ground. The 7x5 "simple" cottage asked for {wood=1406}
  (352 logs) before.
Night:
- Goals.sunDown(): time of day 12500 to 23500, or dark outside. Goals.evening() (from 11000) is still used for "too
  late to start something".
- Dusk branch in the Mind's options: evening, not night, before sunDown, no danger. It is SHELTER when home is 48 to
  400 blocks away ("dusk: heading home before dark"), STONE when it has under NIGHT_BLOCKS blocks and isn't near home
  ("dusk: blocks for a hut tonight"), and otherwise the day goes on. Before, the dark branch started at 11000, and it
  dug in while the sun was up.
Fights:
- Companion.foe(): the last foe it hit stays its foe for 3 s (alive, within 10 blocks, not at peace with it, not a
  creative or spectator player). Next comes a hostile mob within 10 that has it as its target and is in sight
  (nearest first). Then the old checks. Before, foe() could return null between hits, and the chore ran in the gaps.
Mining:
- Choices.unsafeToBreak: under the ground (no sky above), a block with water beside or above it is "water behind it:
  it would flood the tunnel".
Exploring:
- Goals.curiousAbout(): the nearest place in Places within 160 blocks in this dimension that it hasn't seen up close
  (not its own places: home, mine, bed, farm, pen, portal...). exploreStep walks there ("going to see the village").
  Within 10 blocks it counts as seen, and the journal says "explores: had a look at the village". There it looks
  around for 3 to 6 s instead of 1.5 to 4.
Walker (thinking about the way back):
- known(p) is also true for blocks on its way: a LongLinkedOpenHashSet of the blocks its feet and head have been in
  (the last 4000, cleared on a change of dimension), filled every tick by Walker.tick. Before, a dark block more than
  8 blocks away (Manhattan) was planned as stone. Its own staircase down a mine looked like rock to dig through, and
  PILLAR won.
  - Checked: told to go 20 blocks down and back, it went down to y 64. The way up was 35 moves (walk 18, ascend 13,
    pillar 3), and it was at the top in 13 s with the same 34 cobblestone.
- placeWorth(): 2 with dirt, or more than need + 8 stone; otherwise 30. need is 8 for a furnace (no furnace, no iron
  pickaxe) plus 3 under a stone pickaxe. PILLAR and BRIDGE add it. ASCEND that digs stone gives back the +12
  tunnelling reluctance of each stone block when the worth is 30 (the stone is wanted).
- Hands.spareBlock(): it puts down dirt, then cobbled deepslate, then cobblestone. This covers pillaring, bridging,
  place() and placeAt("any").
Names and skins:
- nameStyle "accurate" (the new default) and skins "accurate" (the new default). Config version 10 moves "player" and
  ["blob"] (the old defaults) to them.
  - The accurate name style is real_names.txt first, like "real". A name typed in /xen summon <name> for a Xen not seen
    before is taken as an account's: create(..., typed) waits up to 3 s for its skin (Skins.playerNow, on the common
    pool, not behind the gallery). After that come Names.fresh("player") names, whose skins are never fetched (a made-up name could be a
    stranger's account). Arena names (Red1...) and returning Xens keep their own skins.
  - The accurate skins setting is mineskin.org's gallery (fetched at start), with the modern pack until the gallery is in.
  - Checked: /xen summon jeb_ logged "Xen has jeb_'s skin". A random Xen was "naminel", with a gallery skin.
Benchmark (bench_client.js: 3 Xens at 1250 -820, /tick rate 40, 12 real minutes = 28800 ticks):
- Stone pickaxes at 37 to 42 s. lazy_matcha: furnace 5:01, iron ingot 5:07, iron pickaxe 5:18. neon_maple: furnace
  10:51, iron ingot 10:57. rinaeer was slain by a zombie at 11:37.
- The run before these fixes: no iron, 2 deaths to zombies, one Xen at "making furnace" for 208 s.
- First shelter at 5:09 (time of day about 12400).


WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.6
==========================

talk/Words.java (no game in it; TwoCheck tests it):
- Vocabulary: assets/xen/vocab.json has pron, det, prep, wh, neg, conj, adj and adv; aux (be, do, have, can, will,
  should, must, may); intj (greet, bye, thanks, laugh, yes, no, wow); verbs (root -> s, past, ing, past participle);
  plurals; nouns by kind (animal, mob, person, place, food, thing); and normalize (shorthand and typos to words).
  - XenMod.started adds every ENTITY_TYPE (mob, animal or thing by MobCategory) and ITEM (food when Facts.fills > 0) name
    as a noun. That makes 4153 words in all on 1.21.11.
  - Words it doesn't know get a guessed kind: -ly an adverb; -ing/-ed a verb; after a/the/an adjective/a preposition a
    noun; after a subject with no verb yet a verb; else a noun. They are kept in <world>/xen/words-learned.json (up to
    3000).
- Reading: lower case; its own name taken out; shorthand expanded; two- and three-word nouns joined ("iron golem").
  Each word is tagged by what it can be and the word before it ("mine" after "a" is a noun, after "I" a verb; "like"
  after a subject is a verb, else a preposition).
- parse() gives a Meaning: act (GREET, BYE, THANKS, LAUGH, YES, NO, WOW, ASK, ASK_WH, TELL, COMMAND, OTHER), wh,
  subject, rel, negated and object.
  - A phrase is [det/possessive] [adjectives] noun+, or a pronoun.
  - rel is the verb's root, "be", "at" (be + a place or coordinates), "can X", "adjective + preposition" ("scared
    of"), or "do" ("what do zombies do").
  - The object is a phrase, an adjective, a place ("in the forest", "at 120 64 -30", "at y -58"), "fish and chicken",
    "to swim", or nothing ("pigs can't fly").
- Memory: Fact(subject, subjectText, plural, rel, negated, object, objectText, source, time), at most 400.
  - tell() gives NEW, KNOWN, or CHANGED (told the other way round: the new one replaces the old).
  - recall(subject, rel, object) matches by root (cats = cat), newest first. newTo(other) picks one to share.
- sentence() builds a sentence with agreement:
  - I am / you are / it is / they are; likes vs like; doesn't / don't; isn't / aren't; can / can't;
  - irregular third persons from the verb forms;
  - es/ies otherwise; a/an.
- reply(text, Context):
  - An answer to what it asked: yes/no, or the missing thing ("fish"; "it is a mob"; "it" resolved to the last
    topic).
  - TELL: kept. Its answer depends on whether the fact is NEW, KNOWN, CHANGED, or one the game already knows. About the
    speaker ("I like diamonds"): kept, but the rest of it answers, as before.
  - ASK: from memory, in the asker's words, with who told it. If it knows the subject with another object: "not sure
    about bread, but cats like fish". From the game. Else it asks back ("do they?").
  - ASK_WH: the objects it knows, up to 3, joined with "and"; "what do X do" gives all it knows about X. Then the game.
    Else it asks back and waits 2 minutes for the answer.
  - Anything else (greetings, requests, questions about the Xen itself): null, and the existing parts answer.
- Context.game(subject, rel), in Companion.gameKnows:
  - drop/give: Facts.dropsSaid, from one close by (its loot table), else what's been rolled, else the table;
  - be: Facts.what ("a hostile mob", "an animal", "a sea creature", "food (fills N hunger)", "a block", "an item");
  - at: Places.
Companion.request:
- Words.parse first. A TELL/ASK/ASK_WH whose subject is a thing (not you, I, we, it, this, that, or the Xen) is chat,
  not a request: "cows drop leather" was intent food, "diamonds are at y -58" mine, "wolves eat bones" eat.
- After talker.answer: Words.reply. A TELL "<place> is at x y z" also goes into Places.
- memory is saved in companions.json ("facts").
- Teaching.tick passes on news (a fact the other Xen doesn't know). There is one piece of news per pair every 2
  minutes, on its own timer apart from skill lessons, and the 45 s spacing still holds. Checked: Steve told one Xen
  "zombies burn in the sun", and 45 s later the other Xen answered "what do zombies do?" with it.
Mining:
- Companion.diamondsWatch (every 2 s): with a pickaxe below iron, diamonds seen within 24 go into Places "diamonds"
  (journal "notes", one line said).
  - With an iron pickaxe, free, not busy, within 256 and not out at night: Chores.mineAt(spot). That is
    mine(spot y, diamonds, 3), going to the spot first in cave mode.
  - Checked: a sealed room with deepslate diamond ore and a stone pickaxe gave "notes diamonds at ...". After an iron
    pickaxe it went back and mined them.
- Staircase: the goal is min(down, 3) steps ahead and down. It used to be one point "down" blocks away, which the
  walker could reach by odd digging.
- The stone it digs into when no ore shows reads "digging into the stone to look for ore" (it read "mining stone ore").
Ex1: stays v3.
- v4 (8 recordings, 34254 frames) on the same held-out frames: danger .844 (v3 .819), attack .948 (.932), but sprint
  .720 (.758) and pitch 7.3 (6.9).
- On the spear session alone, sprint was .377 (v3 .61): a practice session, mostly standing and swinging.
- The session: 16 min, 91 swings (45 with a diamond spear). 55 were followed by a hotbar swap within 0.6 s: spear to
  hoe 17, spear to axe 14, axe to spear 5. The fastest came 1 tick later.


WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.5
==========================

Fixes from a recorded play-test (50 min, a player and a friend, 15 Xens):
- Antics.watch(): a dance needs seen >= 10 crouches.
  - seen resets to 0 when a dance starts.
  - danceAgain = now + 600..1200 ticks.
  - The dance line is said at most once in 2400 ticks.
  - Before, two dancing Xens (each other's crouches count) restarted it every tick, each time with a line.
- Antics.greeted(): it crouches back as before (every 600 ticks per person). The hello is said at most once in 2400
  ticks per person (saidHiAt).
- Talker.greet(): no greeting in the first 1200 ticks after it arrives (arrivedAt; it has just introduced itself).
  "I missed you!" only when it has greeted that person before.
- Teaching.tick():
  - the first look comes 120..360 s after it arrives (200 ticks with -Dxen.fastTalk);
  - a lesson or a warning is said only 45 s after the last one by any Xen (static lastLessonMs; 5 s with fastTalk).
- Checked: two Xens with 30 s of crouching at them gave 2 dance lines and 2 hellos (before: about 25 lines in 6 s).
- Xen Ex1 v3: 7 recordings, 24496 frames (575 hurt), held out 6129 (160 hurt), 25 epochs (train.py's default now).
  - Same held-out frames, v2 then v3:
    - sprint .758 -> .775, jump .902 -> .910, forward .922 -> .927;
    - pitch error 7.5 -> 7.3 degrees;
    - danger AUC .765 -> .802.
  - The new session's last fifth: sprint .734 -> .715, danger .712 -> .751.
  - 15 epochs gave danger .804 but sprint .751 and pitch 7.8, so 25 it is.

WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.4.2
============================

- gameplayLogFolder (empty): where gameplay logs are saved.
  - Empty or "default": config/xen/gameplay_logs.
  - A relative path is resolved in the game folder ("gameplay_logs", next to the recorder's).
  - An absolute path is used as is.
- GameplayLog.folder() creates the folder and checks that it can write there. If it can't, it uses the default and
  warns once per value.
- When the setting changes, the open logs close and the next ones start in the new folder.
- Settings screen: "Logs go to" (config/xen/gameplay_logs or gameplay_logs). Any other folder: /xen set.
- Checked on the 1.21.11 test server: a full path with a space, and a folder it can't create (/proc/...), which fell
  back to the default.


WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.4.1
============================

Gameplay logs (GameplayLog.java; setting gameplayLog: off, xens, players, both; default off):
- One JSONL file for each logged Xen and player in config/xen/gameplay_logs: xen_<name>_<time>.jsonl and
  player_<name>_<time>.jsonl. A new file after 200 MB, a new one each time the server starts or the player comes back.
- The gameplay recorder's format 1.2.0, so xen/ex1 reads both the same way.
  - session_start: mod_version 1.2.0, written_by (Mind.VERSION), source (xen or player), who, interval_ticks 5,
    fight_interval_ticks 1.
  - state every 5 ticks, every tick for 3 s after a hurt or a hit. It holds dimension, raining, thundering, day_time,
    screen (a container menu's type, else null), biome and light. The player part has pos, velocity, yaw, pitch,
    look_dir, on_ground, sprinting, sneaking, in_water, health, food, air and xp. Then come input, selected_slot,
    main_hand, off_hand, armor and using_item.
  - inventory every 10 s.
  - looking_at uses its block and entity reach, like a client. Then blocks (below, feet, head) and nearby (16 nearest
    within 24: type, dist, rel, hostile, health, holding).
  - vision every 10 ticks: 14 x 24 rays over 90 x 130.626 degrees to 192 blocks; dist floor or -1; idx a palette
    index, -2 past 64, -1 for a miss; open_frac.
  - Keys:
    - a player's come from ServerPlayer.getLastClientInput() (the input packet game clients send since 1.21.2);
    - a Xen's come from its zza/xxa, jump key, sneak and sprint;
    - attack is "swinging" and use is "using an item".
  - Events:
    - damage_taken: after armor, from ServerLivingEntityEvents.AFTER_DAMAGE. A killing hit has no damage event of its
      own, so died() writes one with "fatal": true before the death.
    - death.
    - swing: AttackEntityCallback for players; Hands for Xens, which have no game client and so no attack packet. The
      cooldown is taken before the hit; target is the type id, as in the recorder.
    - swing at a block: AttackBlockCallback.
    - block_break: PlayerBlockBreakEvents.AFTER, with ticks since the first swing at that block.
    - chat_out and chat_in: heard() and Companion.say; with local chat, only those in range get chat_in.
- A logged player gets one line in chat when their log starts.
- About 30 MB an hour each, more in long fights.
- xen/ex1:
  - features.source(records) reads who played a log.
  - train.load() leaves Xens' own logs out unless --with-xen.
  - compare.py lists side by side (Xens and players, or --each log):
    - moving, sprinting while moving, jumps a minute, sneaking;
    - hits a minute, charge at a hit, fully charged hits, sprint hits, ms to turn to a creature that hit it;
    - damage a minute and from what, deaths;
    - blocks a minute, which blocks, ticks a block;
    - Ex1's forward, sprint and jump accuracy, pitch error and danger AUC on that play.
- Checked on the 1.21.11 test server (a player and a Xen):
  - every event type was written;
  - states came 4 a second, 20 in a fight;
  - train.py and compare.py read the files.
  - The test player (mineflayer) sends no input packet, so its keys read false; a real client sends them.

WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.3
==========================

Xen Ex1 v2:
- Data: 6 recordings. The first is 22 min in the first recorder format. The other 5 sessions are 56 min in recorder
  1.2.0, with a friend, vein mining and tree felling mods, mob fights and some PvP. 15036 frames, 322 of them hurt;
  held out 3764 (112 hurt).
- features.frames() reads both formats.
  - 1.2 records: type "state" (4 Hz, 20 Hz in fights) and type "event" (damage_taken, swing, block_break, block_place,
    slot_changes, chat_in, chat_out, game_message, session_start).
  - A frame at most every 200 ms; none while a screen is open.
  - The turn and the next pitch come from the first state at least 250 ms on.
  - Hurt: a damage_taken event or a health drop over .5 within 2000 ms.
- Held out (the last fifth of each recording), v2 then v1 on the same frames:
  - sprint .773 (.735; always the same .657), jump .918 (.904; .862), forward .926 (always the same .625);
  - pitch error 5.9 degrees (8.1; guess 15.6);
  - danger AUC .787 (.739);
  - yaw .711 (always the same .712: still no better).
- Ex1.fingerprint() = hidden:hash(b1):hash(b2). learned() writes it as "base". restore() refuses a file without the
  same base, and XenMod then keeps that file as ex1-learned.json.old: a danger head learned on v1 would undo v2.

From the recordings:
- Reflexes: unseen +50..150 (was +150..300). A player turned to whoever hit them a median 251 ms after the hit (n 15);
  hitting back took a median 1.2 s (n 7).
- Not copied: against players, the player mostly spam-clicked (charge at a hit: median .08, 5% at .9 or more). Xens keep
  charged hits; their fight genes decide.
- No x-ray in the data: the x-ray the chat talks about was the other player's. The recordings are from the recording
  player's own view, so every ore in them was found fairly.


WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.2
==========================

Xen Ex1 (xen/ex1/, core/Ex1.java, Ex1Senses.java):
- Senses (119), the same in xen/ex1/features.py and Ex1Senses:
  - body: on ground, in water, sprinting, sneaking, health, food, speed, vertical speed, pitch, light, rain, dimension;
  - the blocks below, at the feet and at the head, as air/solid/water/lava/small/other;
  - what it looks at (none/block/entity, distance, block kind, hostile);
  - the nearest monster (closeness, sin/cos of its bearing, height), monsters within 8 and 16, the nearest other
    creature;
  - hand kind and shield, using an item;
  - 7x8 sight lines: rows 2i+1 and columns 3j+1 of the recorder's 14x24 over 90 x 130.6 degrees. Each gives its
    distance over 64; a miss within 64 is 1;
  - lava in view, water share, open share (misses within 192).
- Network: 119 -> 64 -> 64 (tanh). Heads:
  - keys: 9 sigmoids;
  - yaw: 5 bins of the next quarter second's turn (-30, -8, 8, 30);
  - pitch: tanh;
  - danger: a sigmoid for health lost in the next 8 frames.
- Training (numpy, Adam, 15 epochs, weight decay 1e-2, hurt frames weighted to balance) holds out the last fifth of
  each recording. On 4308 frames (141 hurt), held out 1078:
  - sprint .84 (vs .72 always the same), jump .86 (vs .81);
  - pitch error 6.4 degrees (vs 14.0);
  - danger AUC .936;
  - yaw .774 (vs .773: no better yet).
- The weights ship in assets/xen/ex1.json; the fixture test/fixtures/ex1.json checks Java against Python (max
  difference 1e-5).
- In the game, Companion.ex1Step runs every second decision (about 2 a second) and stores ex1Out.
  - A hurt (once a second at most) teaches the danger head the last 5 moments (rate .006).
  - A moment 2.5 s old with no hurt since teaches it "safe" (rate .004).
  - Only the danger head learns; the rest stays as trained. Shared by all Xens; saved as xen/ex1-learned.json.
- Walker:
  - no sprint where Ex1's sprint key is under .25;
  - sprint-jumps on straight walks when Ex1 would jump (with headroom and 4+ moves to go);
  - pitch half the path gaze, half Ex1's pitch.
- Setting: ex1 (on).

Gut.java, learned:
- The amygdala's fear for IDLE, FORWARD, BACK, LEFT, RIGHT, JUMP, and Ex1's danger.
- weigh(): keep = max(fear stay, fear on). It takes the least-feared move when keep >= .15 and
  (keep - least) * caution >= .12, or when danger >= .8 and relief >= .04.
- keepAway(): blocks within 3 that it has an aversion to push it away (1/d^2). It takes the step (forward, back,
  left, right) best aligned with the push, never into a wall or onto one, with fear as a tie-break.
- Each comes a reaction time after it's felt; -Dxen.gutDebug=true writes what it feels every second.
- Removed: the lava, fire and badly-hurt rules of beta.1.

Aversions.java:
- XenPlayer.hurtServer -> aversions.hurt(source).
- Causes:
  - a creature: "mob:<type>";
  - lava;
  - the fire or campfire block under or at it, else "fire";
  - hotFloor -> magma_block, cactus, sweetBerryBush -> sweet_berry_bush, freeze -> powder_snow;
  - falls, hunger and drowning teach nothing here.
- Each hurt adds .3 + .04 * damage (max 1). From .3 it keeps away; it fades x.997 a minute. Saved in companions.json.
- Lava school (3 fresh Xens, 20 rounds, a barrier corridor, lava 2 blocks off flowing toward it): each learned lava
  from its first burn. Hurt in 6% of rounds after that, against 22-33% before aversions.

Teaching.java:
- Xen to Xen (every 20 s, another Xen within 6, once per pair per 10 min):
  - an aversion >= .5 the other lacks: the other learns it (.35, "told by");
  - else a skill 0.25 or more better: the other gains 0.08 * gap * (0.6 + 0.8 * diligence).
- Player to Xen:
  - "stay away from/avoid/don't touch X" or "X burns/hurts/is dangerous" -> aversions (.4);
  - "teach me", "tips", "advice", "how do I get better" -> a tip for the named skill (else its best one); under .35
    it says it's bad at it.
- Fights:
  - the one who hit it (within a minute), within 8 blocks, crouching twice -> judge();
  - chance = .25 + .5 kindness - .4 wrath + .25 trust + .2 composure - .12 (hits - 1) - .15 if aggressive, clamped
    .03 to .95;
  - forgiven: makePeace and +.1 trust; not forgiven: -.05 trust;
  - chat from someone it's fighting (not a truce) gets fight talk.

Sight: Hands.clearTo, Hands.inTheWay, Chores.hitFromHere, Life.visible and Choices.lookingAtWater clip with
COLLIDER (not OUTLINE). Blocks with no collision (leaf litter, glow lichen, grass, flowers, torches) don't block
sight.


WHAT'S NEW IN 2.0.0-beta.1 (XEN 2.0)
====================================

Three brains (Choices.java):
- Every choice is a Weigh filled in by the three brains, then decide():
  - the Doer: want, with a reason;
  - the Doubter: risk, each with a reason; "passing" risks set when to think again;
  - the Gut: the outcome it pictures.
- decide() rules:
  - a hard no: NOT;
  - want >= 0.05 and want - caution * risk > 0.05: DO;
  - a passing risk with want >= 0.15, or wantLater >= 0.3: LATER, until now + later (at most 30 minutes, MAX_LATER);
  - otherwise NOT.
- Caution is Personality.cautionScale() (0.4 for the bravest to 1.6 for the most timid).
- A close call (|score| < 0.08) adds confusion. A confused Xen may flip DO to a 5 s LATER, or LATER to DO; never a
  hard no.
- A LATER is held until its time, unless it's starving.
- Changes of answer go to the journal: "chooses fish: later (in 8 min) | doer: ... | doubter: ... | gut: ...".
- fish(): rod (or 2 string), water (Fisher.waterNear), and its line of sight on water (16 blocks, a source block).
  - Not looking yet: it faces the water and decides 1.5 s later.
  - want = hunger (1, 0.55, 0.25 or 0.05) + liking (0.3 with the fish/kindness beliefs, else 0.12)
    + 0.35 * (angler - 0.3) + rain.
  - Risks: night or dusk (0.6, until morning; less for night owls); monsters within 16; busy (8 min); hurt.
  - Plenty of food: later, in 15 min.
  - Used by Fisher.fancies(), starving() (no animal within 16), Goals.food() (no animal close: anyone fishes), and
    choices.moment() (every 5 s when free with nothing on).
  - While fishing, keepFishing() every 3 s stops it at dark or with a monster within 10 ("I'll fish later").
- mine(pos), for every block around it:
  - Hard no:
    - air or fluid;
    - unbreakable;
    - built, chest, spawner or crop;
    - unsafeToBreak: Chores.lavaBehind, or the block under its feet with fluid or 3+ air under it.
  - worth(): diamond/debris 1, emerald .6, iron .8 (under 24), coal .6 (under 16), gold .4, lapis .3, redstone .25,
    copper .08, logs .5, stone .35 (under 32 cobble), dirt .05, leaves 0.
  - Times the hidden pickiness: ore 0.85..1.15x, the rest 1.3..0.5x.
  - Times shape(dy, side), from the recorded game (95 blocks broken):
    - feet or head level 1, one down .7, two up .5, more .25;
    - farther than one block to the side .6x;
    - straight down .3x.
  - Risks:
    - pickaxe tier too low: LATER 10 min (tierNeeded: coal 1; iron, copper, lapis 2; gold, redstone, diamond,
      emerald 3; debris, obsidian 4);
    - water beside it .3;
    - gravel or sand above .15;
    - a monster within 6 .25;
    - over 6 s to break .2.
  - Used by Chores.oreWithinReach and Chores.whileItSmelts.
  - bestToMine(r) ranks every visible block within r.
  - Hands.startMining refuses any dig unsafeToBreak calls a hard no (cantMine).
- animal(e):
  - Hard no: a baby, a named animal or one on a lead.
  - Facts.drops (the loot table rolled 48 times) gives the hunger cooked. want = hunger need * hunger/12 + wool need.
  - Wool need: .7 with no bed and under 3 wool. Shearable with shears: shear instead. A sheared sheep holds none.
  - Risks:
    - the last 1 or 2 of its kind within 16 (.5, unless starving);
    - fences on 2+ sides (.6);
    - a monster next to it (.3, 30 s).
  - Not hungry and no wool need: later, 10 min.
  - Chores.nearestAnimal takes only a yes (or anything at food 6 or less) and journals the pick. huntNext shears when
    choices.shearInstead().
- eat(): later (5 s) with a monster within 4 while health >= 10 and food > 6; the instinct eats only on a yes.

Facts.java (the RAG store):
- drops(entity): LivingEntity.dropFromLootTable(level, playerAttack(xen), false, key, consumer), 48 rolls.
  - Gives item -> {mean, chance}; wool colours are merged; empty stacks are skipped.
  - Cached per kind (a sheared sheep is its own kind).
  - Falls back to a vanilla table.
- fills(item): the item's FOOD component (nutrition); cooked(raw) names; hunger(drops).
- Fishing: about 17.5 s a bite (0.8x in rain); 85% fish (60% cod, 25% salmon); catchesIn(minutes), fishHunger().
- TIPS: one-line lessons, found by about(topic).

Gut.java (survival override): Companion.instinct() calls gut.override() first. Each case starts a reaction time
after it's noticed:
- in lava: faces the nearest standable block within 5, sprints, Action.JUMP;
- lava beside its feet (same level, or an edge down to lava it's moving toward): faces the lava, Action.BACK;
- on fire, not in water: walks into water within 6;
- health 6 or less with a monster (not a creeper) within 5: 4 s backing off (6 blocks away, sprinting), at most every
  30 s, then eats if it can.
- Says so once (30 s) when it breaks off something it was asked. Journal: "gut takes over: ...".

Reflexes.java:
- sampleMs: log-normal around 230 ms (sigma .22).
  - Unseen: +50..150 (beta.2: +150..300).
  - Tired (night, 15+ min awake): +40.
  - Confusion: +180 * level.
  - Focused (in a fight): -50.
  - Clamped to 120..750, then times the setting (fast .7, slow 1.4, instant 0) and the hidden reflexes
    (1.25 - .5 * reflexes).
- ready(key, unseen): true once the reaction time since it first saw key has passed. Keys are forgotten after 10 s.
- Used by:
  - fightBack: a new foe that hasn't hurt it yet;
  - Fisher: the bite;
  - the Gut.
- Hands.turnToward eases like a mouse: a step of min(max, 0.6 * left + 1.5) degrees, times turnScale().

Confusion.java:
- level 0..1.
- Goes up with:
  - closeCall +.05;
  - surprise: a hit from out of view .12, respawn .3;
  - each second: dark +.012 (less for night owls), 3+ monsters +.02, health 6 or less +.015.
- Everything is times the setting (off 0, low .5, high 1.5) and 1.5 - composure.
- Settles .02 a second (.01 in a fight).
- flips(): from level .3, up to 1 in 5, less when stubborn.
- step(), between chores, never in a fight: from .35 a look around (0.5 to 2 s). From .6, now and then a question
  ("wait... which way?", once every 2 minutes).

Hidden stats (Personality.hidden):
- reflexes, composure, humor, typing, appetite, pickiness, angler, night owl, stubborn.
- Each N(0.5, 0.22) clipped to 0..1. Given in bornWith() (an older Xen: from its name), mixed and mutated in
  child(), saved as "hidden".
- Never in its status or its talk. The journal notes them once at birth ("hidden: quick reflexes, a joker, ...").
- Appetite shifts eatAt (+-2) and its sense of hunger (+-2 food).

Talk:
- talk/Texting.casual(line, casual, random), applied to every line said (Companion.say, Talker.sayNear):
  - always: decimals with units rounded; contractions;
  - by casualness (the hidden typing stat; cheerful and silly more, calm less): gonna, wanna, gotta, ok, tbh, idk,
    rn, cuz, prob, thx, u;
  - no final period, no capital, now and then "lol" or "ngl".
- Voice.reply:
  - banter (an insult in capitals or with lol, lmao, jk, haha, xd) gets a joke back, chance .35 + humor;
  - short reactions ("lol", "true", "damn", "fr"...) get a short one back;
  - Texting.slangPraise ("peak", "fire", "W build", "goated"...) counts as praise.
- Remarks: no percentages and no "Can I tell you something?". The remark openers are now ngl, honestly, ok so,
  lowkey, tbh.
- "What are you doing?" reads right (Talker.saidDoing: "I'm looking around, no animals in sight").
- chatter(): unprompted lines at least talkGapMillis apart (talkAmount: quiet 120 s, normal 45 s, chatty 20 s, or
  the personality's own gap if longer). "Always" lines at least 8 s apart outside a conversation.
- Signs:
  - note() at most every 2.5 min (was 5);
  - with no sign it orders one sign recipe (6 planks + a stick = 3 signs), once every 10 min;
  - back at where it died: "I died here (<what>). Careful.".

Skins and names:
- "blob" (the default in beta 1 to 6, "accurate" since beta 7; config version 9 moved "modern" to "blob"): 24 simple flat-colour skins from
  scripts/make_blob_skins.py, signed through mineskin.org, in assets/xen/skins/blob.json.
- nameStyle "real": the first untaken name in config/xen/real_names.txt (created with notes on first use); that
  account's skin from Mojang's profile API (fetched at start for every listed name).

Settings (Xen 2.0 tab): reaction (human), confusion (human), talkAmount (normal), signs, gameplayLog (off; beta.4.1).

Checks: TwoCheck (in crossCheck) covers:
- the facts and the weighing of choices;
- the mining shape and pickaxe tiers;
- reaction times (median 230 ms, unseen +50..160, fast and confused);
- typing (decimals, careful vs casual, coordinates kept, slang praise);
- hidden stats (born, saved, inherited, given to old Xens, never described).


WHAT'S NEW IN 1.9.3
===================

Standing about:
- Goals.agenda, dark: with a pickaxe (tier 1+) and MINE allowed, the night's for mining, above ground too.
  - Reasons in the journal: "night: mining" (underground or near its mine), "digging down from its shelter", or
    "digging down to mine".
  - The old wantsOre() gate is gone at night.
  - Only the belief night_belongs_to_monsters keeps it in (above ground). Then, sheltered or home, it crafts, smelts
    or stores, else rests; out in the open it builds a shelter.
- Companion.standingAbout: idle with no chore (instant empty, "looking around" or "exploring") moves on after 400
  ticks (was 1200; a chore still gets 1200).
  - Moving on is Goals.exploreFor(900): option EXPLORE with the Short EXPLORE goal (was a random 16-block walk).
  - At its furnace (SMELT) counts as busy.
- Chores.smeltNext, while waiting (checkFurnaceAt): whileItSmelts() mines the best natural block in reach. It looks
  from its level to 2 up, within 4 blocks, visible: ore, then stone/deepslate/cobblestone, then logs. Never the
  furnace or what's under it.
- Critters.danger: a ranged mob targeting it, not drawing, in sight.
  - Armed and health 10+ (or health 16+ and brave): it walks in and hits between shots.
  - Otherwise it runs 14 blocks away from it.

Requests:
- "explore" is Goals.exploreAsked(3 min): drop(), begin(Short.EXPLORE), option EXPLORE, exploreAskedUntil. Until then:
  - nightfall() doesn't drop it;
  - progressWaiting doesn't cut it short;
  - exploreStep doesn't head home at dusk or turn to tunnel mining underground (it goes up and out);
  - bedBeforeNight leaves it alone.
- Chat.understand: a line starting with an order verb (go, get, build, mine, explore...) loses a trailing "?".
- Companion.GO_PLACE: "go/walk/head/run/take me/lead me/bring me (back) to/into (the) <place>" goes through
  goToPlace(kind), which sets commandedTo:
  - cave: Caves.nearest(400), else Places "cave";
  - home/house/base: goals.home;
  - mine, portal (or ruined portal), temple (desert or jungle), monument, outpost, mansion, trial chamber, village,
    stronghold...: Places.
  - Owner, or trust 0.5+.

Placing:
- Hands.placeAt clicks any clickable neighbour (not air, not replaceable, a non-empty shape), not only full blocks.
- It sneaks when clicking an interactive block (containers, tables, doors, trapdoors, gates, buttons, levers, diodes,
  anvils, beds).
- Hands.placeSupported(pos, material, underOk): with nothing to put a block against, it puts one under it first (down
  to 3 below, where underOk allows).
- Chores.shelterNext:
  - uses placeSupported, never filling the room's own columns;
  - after 12 stuck ticks it walks to another cell inside (as many tries as cells);
  - after 30, at night, with a pickaxe or diggable ground, it switches to pitPlan (a hole two deep with a lid) instead
    of giving up.
- Chores.shelter: under the ground (no sky above) with a pickaxe, it digs a pit first, not a hut.
- Chores.glance (gathering): blocks below its feet cost 1.5 per block down, and +8 in the 3x3 column under it. It takes
  faces at its own level first instead of a crater round its feet.

Chat:
- Companion keeps a Talk per player: last and previous line, last question, its subject (Voice.subject), its own last
  answer (recorded in say() while talkingWith).
- Voice.followUp, within 3 minutes:
  - "what about / how about / and / also X" swaps X into the last question for its subject. It keeps the plural
    unless X is a mass word, and skips pronouns and verbs.
  - "(...,) and you / wbu / hbu / what about you": liking a topic is "do you like <topic>?", "I'm ..." is "how are
    you?" or "what are you doing?".
  - A question with it/that/them and no subject of its own gets the last subject.
  - The request is re-read with Chat.understand (journal: "follow-up: ... means ...").
- The chat model's notes start with the exchange before ("Just before, X said ... and you answered ...").
- Lines about oneself ("I love/like/hate/found/got/have/made/saw/think X") aren't gathering orders.
- Chat.firstPerson: you'll/you've/you'd become I'll/I've/I'd, and "you can/could/should/want/..." becomes "I ...", not
  "me ...". The goal texts say "smelt the iron", "put things away".
- Grudges:
  - Diplomacy.asked outside a fight with negative trust mends it by 0.25 + 0.35 kindness - 0.25 wrath (at least 0.1,
    at most up to +0.05), and says whether it forgives.
  - Every 5 minutes negative trust fades by 0.02 + 0.05 kindness - 0.02 wrath.
  - The refusal adds "(a sorry would help)".
- CrossCheck adds follow-ups 6/6, "go explore?" and "get some wood?", and the first-person cases.


WHAT'S NEW IN 1.9.2
===================

Tools (Hands). selectBestTool(state) before every dig:
- It looks over all 36 slots for the item with the highest destroy speed above 1.0. A sword counts only on cobweb or
  bamboo. On a tie, the hotbar wins.
- A backpack tool is swapped into the hotbar first: an empty slot 0-7, else a slot without a damageable item, else 7.
- If nothing beats a bare hand, it holds an empty or non-damageable slot rather than wear a tool out.
- The slot is kept to the end of the block: digSlot is restored every tick, and again at the very end of the Xen's tick
  (Hands.keepTool). Its player ticks before its mind, so a later switch in the same tick was what others saw.
- ready() won't switch while digging.
- If the item in the dig slot changes (handed a sword into the empty slot it was punching with), it picks again.
- Crafter.wanted() also makes a stone shovel once it has stone tools.

Beds (Companion):
- noticeSheep(), every second, remembers the nearest sheep in view (or within 12 blocks) and the time.
- bedBeforeNight(), in the instinct chain right after starving, applies when all of these hold: in the overworld, free,
  not building, not asked for something, no bed or bed item, fewer than 3 wool.
  - Late day (8500-12500) or night: every 5 s, it hunts sheep it can see. The range is 40 blocks by day. At night it is
    16 blocks, and only with fear <= 0.5, health >= 12 and no monster within 12.
  - Late day with none in sight: it walks to the sheep it saw within the last 5 minutes and 96 blocks. The trip is kept
    for up to 90 s, then it hunts the sheep there.
- Chores.hunt with forWool counts wool, not food. It only goes after sheep, picks up wool drops, and gives up after
  30 s with no sheep.
- A "bed" intent (get/find/collect wool, wool for, make/craft/need a bed) runs bedAsked(). It crafts the bed if it has
  3 wool, else it hunts the sheep nearby or walks back to where it saw some.

Beds, the rest of the way:
- Crafter.wanted() makes the bed (bedFromWool: 3 wool of one colour, with 3 planks + 4 for a table if none is near),
  crafted at once like tools.
- next() plans a bed's planks (3, no sticks), not a tool's.
- With the wool but not the wood (bedNeedsWood), bedBeforeNight gathers 2 logs.
- bedErrandUntil, and a wool hunt, stop Goals.think from starting something over it.
- bedtime() looks for room within 2 blocks: both halves free and dry, solid under both, any of 4 ways. The agenda only
  camps (REST "night: it camps with its bed") where there's room.
- Xen 2.0 choices set chores.own (its own idea). Before, everything it chose looked like a player's request, and the
  bed check never interrupted it. It may also interrupt its own house (Builder.ownHouse); chores run before the builder,
  so the build waits.

Nights (Goals.agenda, dark):
- A Xen tier >= 1 in its shelter (or a hut it built below ground) goes mining when it wants ore.
- Sheltered or within 24 blocks of home, it crafts, smelts or stores before REST.
- Crafter:
  - An order that lacks sticks and has no planks makes planks first.
  - A failed order it chose itself sets nextTry to 30 s later.
  - MindSense only allows CRAFT when crafter.canTry().
- Goals.thinkMind: a choice (other than eat or flee) that is over in under 2 s is barred for 20 s (quickUntil). This
  stops the three-times-a-second loops.
- Crafter.next() does nothing but pick its table back up until nextTry: a table it had put down used to keep it
  "ready" and retrying a failing craft.
- Chores HIDE (a shelter for the night, its own idea, not following anyone): after 20 s, fed (8+), health 12+, pickaxe
  tier 1+, it starts mine() from where it is, down to the depth it believes in for coal/iron/diamonds. At most once
  per 3 minutes.

Chat that acts (talk/Chat.understand):
- A suggestion or polite lead-in is stripped, and the rest is matched against the request rules. Lead-ins: why
  don't/not you or we, why not, how about (you/we), maybe you/we should/could, you/we should/could/can/need to,
  (do you) want/wanna (to), shall we, should we/you, can/could we, would/will/could/can you, try to.
- A rest starting with what/who/where/when/how many stays a question.
- "should I ..." stays chat (advice, answered below).
- The requests then run as usual: owner rules, refusals, ack in its tone.

Harder questions (talk/Voice):
- hear() sets ask/about/other: recipe (how do I make/craft/get/find, what do I need for, recipe for), should (should
  I/we, is it a good idea to), next (what should we/I do, what now, what's next, the plan, tonight), friend, going,
  lately, safe, compare ("X or Y", with better/prefer/... cut away), why (why + about it or that, how come).
- reply() answers these before the network, from Voice.Self defaults (the game fills them in):
  - why(): who asked it, else the agenda's reason or why its mind chose that option, in first person.
  - next(): its next step as a verb phrase.
  - bestFriend(): the highest trust above 0.3 among players and Xens, else its owner.
  - lately(): its last 3 finished choices, from Goals.done.
  - danger(): 0.3 per monster within 16, +0.3 if hurt.
  - night()
- Recipes and where to find things: talk/HowTo, about 80 entries. "Which is better": HowTo.better() facts, else
  material tiers, else like().
- Companion.request asks the Voice first for these, in both modes (own words or chat model), before SmallTalk.
- Voice.hear also marks "you should/why don't you/..." as suggestions for it: an ACCEPT says "I'll ..." not "let's ...".
- CrossCheck: 11/11 harder questions answered and 11/11 suggestions and asks mapped, besides the 1.9.1 checks.


WHAT'S NEW IN 1.9.1
===================

Its own words (talk/Lexicon, talk/ActNet, talk/Voice). Used when the chat model isn't loaded (off, auto without the
memory, still loading): Companion.request, after the requests and the grounded answers (Talker.answer; SmallTalk for
everything but chit-chat), says Voice.reply(speaker, said, grounded, learn). grounded is Chat.plainly's answer when the
line is a question about a thing it might have or have seen (not an opinion question).

Lexicon: assets/xen/words.json (or config/xen/words.json): normalize (chat shorthand -> words, some to several words),
polarity (-2..2 per word), topics (about 100: cat, like -1..1, plural or mass, article, verb, pos and neg predicates that
fit "<topic> is/are ___"), word pools (about 45: greet, bye, agree, dunno, love, hate, very, laugh, care, proud, hurt by
temper, ask back, accept, decline, ack...) where "word|tone,tone" is three times as likely for those tones and a fifth
as likely for others, and the last 24 words it used a tenth as likely; jokes; styles per tone (end mark, chance of an
extra one, a smiley, lower case, a stammer, trailing off, hedging).

Reading (Voice.hear): its name out, letters repeated 3+ times cut to 2, words normalized; question (a "?" or a wh- or
auxiliary first word); flags: greet, bye, thanks, sorry, praise (about you and good, or "good job"), insult (about you
and bad, or an insult word), laugh, yes/no (short), how are you, what are you doing, like-question (do you like, think
of/about, feel about, favorite, opinion), suggestion (let's, we should, shall we, want to...? and the next 5 words),
feel-me (I'm/I feel + a good or bad word), news (I found/got/built/made/killed/beat/died, guess what), confused, tell me;
polarity summed with "not/don't/never..." within two words turning it round; the first topic named ("mine" and a bare
"end" skipped).

ActNet: 43 inputs (1, 16 flags, question/statement, has topic, topic liked/disliked by it (>0.3/<-0.3), sounds
good/bad, about you/me, chattiness, curiosity, kindness, bravery, temper x3, tone x6, trust in the speaker, mood good/
bad, busy) -> 32 ReLU -> 18 replies (greet, bye, welcome, feeling, doing, opinion, agree, disagree, ask back, react,
joke, care, proud, hurt, dunno, share, accept, decline). Trained at first start (6000 made-up situations, 12 epochs,
about 0.3 s) on a teacher's reply weights (Voice.teach), saved to config/xen/words.net (8 KB); agrees with the teacher's
favourite 95.9% on new situations. Picking: probabilities cubed, only replies that fit (an opinion needs a topic,
accept/decline a suggestion...), sampled. Learning: the next line from the same player within 90 s is a reward (+1
laugh, praise, thanks, yes; -1 insult, confused; +-0.5/-0.3 by how it sounds; +0.2 otherwise), a policy-gradient step
(lr 0.01) on the reply it gave; Xens talking to each other don't teach it.

Building the reply: each kind of reply is a few sentence shapes filled from the pools, the topic's own predicates, and
what's true of it (Voice.Self: mood from its emotions, hurt, hungry, what it's doing (goals.instant, first person),
its dream, the last place it found, what it thinks of a topic: the topic's like + its nature (greed for ores, bravery
and wrath for monsters, kindness for animals, curiosity for places, skills for building/mining/farming, gluttony for
food, sloth against work) + a fixed +-0.25 of its own per topic). A chatty Xen may add a second sentence on the same
subject (ask back, or about itself). Then it's written in its tone (end marks, stammer, lower case, smiley,
trailing off, contractions). Greeting plus "how are you" gets both. Requests: Voice.ack rewrites "Okay! ..." and
"I can't ..." with its tone's word. Chat.understand's gathering intents (mine, wood, stone, iron, coal, food) are
dropped for news and feelings ("I found diamonds!"). Talker: when two Xens chat (85%), one says Voice.opener (a
question, an opinion, its news, a joke), the other Voice.reply()s to it, and a chatty first one may answer that; 30%
of its own remarks come from Voice.remark() when there's no chat model. CrossCheck: agreement >= 90%, 16 lines read
right, 96 replies in 6 tones well formed and varied, learning moves the reply, save/load round trip.


WHAT'S NEW IN 1.9.0
===================

Eyes on its work (Hands). mine(pos): seePoint() is the block's middle, or the middle of a face turned toward the eyes
(0.45 out), with a clip from the eyes (OUTLINE: grass and flowers count, as a click would hit them) that hits nothing
or that block. None: the first thing in the way (clip to the middle) is dug instead if natural() (ores, stone family,
dirt family, sand, gravel, clay, snow, leaves, plants and other replaceable non-fluids, terracotta, sandstone...) and
reachable and not too slow; else cantMine = pos with cantMineUnseen (Builder: tried again in 2 s, and after 3 tries
blindOk lets it through, as with placing). Aim: if already within 12 degrees it digs at once, else it turns first,
40 degrees yaw and 30 pitch a tick at most (turnToward), up to 16 ticks, then starts. A dig with under 15% progress
after 60 ticks (swimming, in the air) stops with cantMine/cantMineUnseen. Placing: placeAt tries the faces it can see
(canSee) first, by feel only right by its feet (the 3x3 around it from one below to one above) or with blindOk;
placeItem needs sight unless strictSight is off and it's by its feet or blindOk; place() (the small brain) the same.
After a click it holds its eyes on the spot (holdLook: 8 ticks after placing, 6 after using a block; eased 30/25
degrees a tick) unless it moves or watches someone; before, look() snapped back to its cardinal facing the next tick.
Pillaring looks straight down. Crafting prep looks at the table when there is one. Measured with a client watching
every block change near a Xen (angle between its view, sampled over 300 ms, and the block; a raycast for sight):
placing more than 30 degrees off 15 of 103 (crafting tables 100+) -> 0-1 of 25-63, median 1-2; breaking median 4 ->
1; through a block 2 of 255 -> 0.

At sea (Companion.backToShore, Goals.seaThatWay). In water with nothing to stand on 2 blocks under it and 6 of 8
points 6 blocks out water (openWater), unless its walk ends on dry land within 24 or it follows a swimming friend: it
drops what it was doing, turns its exploring round, and swims to nearestLand (rings out to 160 blocks, 3 apart to 48
then 8; surface above sea level and at most 5 over it, and 5 of 8 points 2 blocks round it dry), else lastDry (the
last ground it stood on, within 300), else 64 blocks toward the world spawn; a new target every 40 s or once there.
Exploring: a direction into unloaded land is skipped when half or more of the loaded samples along it (every 8 blocks)
are water. The first look around doesn't happen in water or off the ground, and a direction with a jump of more than
12 in the ground height counts as risky.

Pickups (Companion.pickValue, pickUpNearby, backForMyThings, Chores.dropToPickUp). Value: 10 diamond, emerald,
netherite, ancient debris, totem, elytra, golden apples, heavy core, trial keys; 7 any tool, weapon or armor; 6 iron,
gold, pearls, eyes, blaze and breeze rods, obsidian, books, lapis, coal, name tags, saddles; 4 food; 2 the rest.
Score value / (1 + 0.25 distance); it keeps its current target unless another scores twice as much. Chores: the one
it's going for first, else what it came for, then the nearest.

No standing about (MindSense.allowed, Goals). REST only at night, below 8 health, below 14 when fed 18+ (it heals),
or told to stay; not twice running by day (lastOption). In the day the plan steps aside only for real danger
(DANGER > 0.2), a friend in need or its village under attack (before: whenever FIGHT or FLEE was allowed, which a
rival merely in sight made so). Below 14 health and under 18 food: eat, else get food. MindSense.enemy: no bully or SMP
picks before 3 minutes in the world (age()), and a bully doesn't pick on its own village.

Ready for the worst (Prepared, Storage.stash). Goals.trip() wraps MINE (iron; diamonds = deep), EXPLORE and
ADVENTURE: fewer than 3 meals -> FOOD (at most every 8 min); explore/adventure with fewer than 16 cobblestone+dirt ->
STONE (same); MINE with one pickaxe, 3 cobblestone and sticks or wood -> a quiet order for a stone pickaxe; deep or
adventure, with a home chest within 128, at most every 10 min -> Storage.stash() and STORE ("its valuables left at
home first"). stash deposits STASH items (diamond, emerald, gold ingot/raw, netherite, ancient debris, enchanted book,
lapis, name tag, saddle, experience bottle, mineral blocks, heart of the sea, nautilus shell, trident, elytra), iron
ingots over 10, and spare tools (by kind it keeps the best by material, +0.5 enchanted: two pickaxes, one of the
rest). On death Prepared.died(); once its things aren't lying there any more (lostAt null) and its pickaxe tier is
under 2, Companion asks Prepared.next() (free, or on its own build) before any leftover job: Storage.take() the best
pickaxe, a sword if it has none, 8 food if it has under 3, one at a time from chests it remembers; nothing there:
it starts over. The STORE option leaves a storage job already running alone.

Fixes. Crafter: every step of an ordered craft uses the order id as the goal (it alternated between "wooden hoe" and
"wooden_hoe", so each step counted as a new recipe: 14-26 ticks and a journal line each time). takeTableAlong: not in
the water, and at most 3 tries.


WHAT'S NEW IN 1.8.0
===================

Purpose (Purpose, Goals.bias, Laws). role(): the job Laws gave it ("miner of <tribe>"), else a noun for its Strategy
plan; purpose(): Strategy.WORDS[plan]; goal: set whenever an option starts (the agenda's reason up to its bracket, or
Mind.SAYS). Purpose.style(leader): BUILDER for a builder plan (or a proud settler), CAUTIOUS for survivor/settler,
AMBITIOUS for speedrun/miner/explorer/warrior unless cautionScale > 1.35, else by caution (> 1.1) and pride.
follows() = 0.25 + 0.5 loyalty + 0.35 max(0, trust in the leader), times (0.35 + 0.5 loyalty) when its plan clashes with
the style (cautious vs speedrun/warrior/explorer, ambitious vs survivor/settler, builder vs speedrun/explorer), halved
for a loner, 1 for the leader. lean(): per style, e.g. cautious SHELTER +0.2, SLEEP +0.1, FOOD +0.15, GUARD +0.1,
EXPLORE -0.15, ADVENTURE -0.2 (ambitious MINE +0.2, EXPLORE +0.15, ADVENTURE +0.2, REST -0.1; builder HOUSE +0.25,
WOOD +0.15, STONE +0.1, FARM +0.1), times follows(), added in Goals.bias. Laws: on a new day, when the leader's style
changes it says it, and job fit gets +0.15..0.2 for the jobs the style needs (farmer/guard, miner, builder/woodcutter).

After stone tools (Goals.afterStone, pickTier == 2). Candidates IRON, FOOD, BED, HOME, EXPLORE, each open only if it
can be done (iron < 3 and MINE allowed; meals < 8; no bed, wool < 3, a sheep within 48; no home, not "a hole is
enough"; EXPLORE allowed). Scores: iron 0.55 + 0.35 (miner/speedrun/warrior) + 0.25 (a cave within 160) + 0.3 (sure of
iron - 0.3) + 0.25 (mine skill - 0.5) + 0.15 greed + 0.1 per earlier choice; food 0.2 + 0.5 (1 - meals/8) + 0.2 (hunger
< 14) + 0.25 (settler/survivor) + 0.15 gluttony + 0.2 (farm skill - 0.5); bed 0.3 + 0.3 evening + 0.2 sheep in sight +
0.25 (survivor/settler) + 0.2 (cautionScale - 1) + 0.2 ("night belongs to monsters"); home 0.25 + 0.5 (builder/settler)
+ 0.25 (build skill - 0.5) + 0.15 pride + 0.1 (32+ wood) - 0.4 speedrun - 0.3 (someone else's base here); explore 0.1 +
0.45 curiosity + 0.35 (explorer/trader) + 0.15 (no cave or village known) + 0.15 lust. Each + the leader's lean for
it (cautious food +0.25, bed +0.3, explore -0.2; ambitious iron +0.3, explore +0.2; builder home +0.35), times
follows(), - 0.3 per time it was chosen before, + N(0, 0.12). It keeps the pick until done or 8000/3600/3600/12000/
2400 ticks (food: done at 6 meals), then scores again. Logged as "stone tools, what next? ...". If the group's
favourite differs, it may say so (once a day at most). The old opportunistic wool-for-a-bed step is skipped at tier 2.

Lessons (Lessons). Per subject (iron 16 +-10, diamonds -58 +-7, coal 44 +-14): value, the prior it had before its own
finds, source (BORN, EXPERIENCE, XEN, PLAYER), sure, teacher, confirmed, contradicted, the last 24 heights it found
that ore at. Born: true + N(0, spread / (1 + 0.5 generation)), sure 0.3. found(ore, y) (Hands, on breaking an _ore):
within 10 of the prior confirms it (twice: +0.03 trust in the teacher), more than 20 off contradicts it; value =
(1 - w) prior + w mean(finds), w = n/(n + 3); sure = min(0.95, (1 - w) priorSure + w (0.4 + 0.5 n/(n + 4))); after 3
finds far (> 12) from the prior the source becomes EXPERIENCE. told(subject, y, source, by, theirSure, trust): take =
theirSure (0.3 + 0.7 trust) (1 - 0.6 sure), x0.3 once it has 3 finds of its own. Players: "<ore> ... y/level/at <n>"
in a request. Xens: in a chat either one passes on a belief that differs from the other's by 8 or more: earned (2+
finds, or confirmed) at its confidence, or hearsay (taught by a player or Xen, sure >= 0.55) at 0.7 of it. depth()
feeds Goals, Nether, Adventure and the mine it digs. Saved with the Xen ("lessons").

A first look around (Habits.scout, pickScout, glance, turnHead). On joining (and respawning) it picks among 8
directions (its facing + k*45 +- 15): along the ray every 2 blocks to the reach (10-16; 10 after dying) the surface
(MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES) counts lava +10, water +1.2, a drop over 3 +2 + 0.3/block, a climb over 2 +0.6, an unloaded
chunk +5; at the end animals within 12 (0.25 each, up to 4) and 6 sampled columns (leaves/logs +0.12, bare stone
+0.1); ahead +0.2, + U(0, 0.3). Under a roof, at night, or every way worse than -3: no walk. It walks there (the
walker's stroll: no sprinting but gap jumps) for up to 15 s. Every 14-31 ticks its eyes go for 8-15 ticks to a living
thing in sight within 24, or one of 8 sampled surface blocks within 16 (trees, water, stone, sand, lava), or (15%)
over a shoulder (+-115 degrees). Only the head turns (yHeadRot = yRot + an offset eased 35% a tick, clamped to +-70;
the pitch eases too), after the walker has set the body, so its path doesn't change. Then Goals.thinkNow().

Pace (Pace). craftPrep(step, goal) before every crafting step (Crafter.step, and an order's final craft): a new step
of the same thing 3-6 ticks; the first step of something it has made before 4-8, of something new 14-26 ("works out
the recipe"); IDLE with its eyes down till then. Under pressure (fighting, health < 8, in water or lava, falling over 2
blocks, a Monster within 8) no wait. crafted(): the step is done; a finished tool gets a 6-10 tick look. Its main hand
is watched every tick: a damageable tool with 3 or fewer uses left gone from the same slot = broken: 8-16 ticks
looking at its hands, a line (75%), then the crafter (before chores) makes another if it can. Known recipes are
saved ("crafted"). An order counts its steps only when a step runs (the wait no longer used up its 12 tries).

Fixes. Crafter.wanted(): with no pickaxe, cobblestone and sticks (and a table) but no planks, a stone pickaxe (before,
nothing: it went for wood). Chores: a gather job gives up for want of a pickaxe only when it can't make one good
enough (canMakeAtLeast). Hands.edgeAhead(): a plain step or strafe (not the walker, which has its own guard) toward a
drop of 5 or more with no water stops at the edge.


WHAT'S NEW IN 1.7.1
===================

Chat thread (talk/Chat). The chat is made once per game, but a world closing called close(), which shut its executor
down for good (ExecutorService.shutdownNow is final); the next world opened in the same game submitted to the dead
executor and the RejectedExecutionException went up through the server tick (Chat.sleep from XenMod.wakeChat, or
Chat.ask from chat). Now worker() makes a new single-thread executor when there's none or the last was shut down, and
submit() never throws (it retries once on a fresh executor, else drops the job: ask() gives back its pending slot,
sleep() closes the model on the calling thread). close() also drops the model reference (it kept a closed model
before) and bumps a generation, so a model that finishes loading after its world closed is closed, not kept.
XenMod.tick wraps the whole tick (a RuntimeException is logged at most once a minute, the tick goes on), wakeChat and
the chat-message hook each in their own guard. CrossCheck: "chat across worlds" asks, rests and closes three times.

Walking (Walker.steer, arrived, floorOnceDug, plan). The body yaw aims at the step it's on, or at the next once it's
within half a block of it or moving away from it (in the air, or overshot within 1.2 blocks; not after a knockback);
before, it always aimed at the step's centre, so mid-jump or mid-fall it turned right round and braked. The pitch looks
at the path 3 steps ahead at 1.5 above the ground (never nearer than 2 blocks, -30..35 degrees, eased 30% a tick);
before, a point 1.2 above the step it was on (steeply down when close). A running step (walk, diagonal, straight on)
counts as reached by its column up to 2 blocks up (mid-jump); on foot, standing on the next step's column (within a
block of height) skips to it, unless that's a gap jump, a bridge or a tower, or this step had digging. ASCEND moves are
offered when the block to stand on can be dug out (floorOnceDug: the block under it firm, it and the one above
diggable); before, only a block over its own head could be dug, so at a wall two high the search found nothing, the
solver backed it off five blocks and it came back. With nothing better than where it stands, a search may go on to
4 x 2500 nodes. On a test course (flat, a 2-block drop, a 2-high wall), per run: facing against its motion 27-30 ticks
-> 0-1, looking more than 45 degrees down ~310 of ~490 moving ticks -> 0-3, backing off at the wall 3 of 6 runs -> 0 of
10, 26.4 s -> ~21.5 s. -Dxen.walkDebug=true logs every step, plan and "no way" (development only).

Settings: the Brain choice shows Mind.VERSION (Xen 6.0).


WHAT'S NEW IN 1.7.0
===================

Houses (TimberHouse, Architect.designed(..., stage)). A cottage (any roof asked of the COTTAGE style) is built by
TimberHouse from Parts: a footprint (u0..u1, v0..v1), a roof whose ridge runs along v or u, whether its front row is a
